metadata.description: IDL 2026 Week 7 KP04; reasoning-led-teaching-deck 2.1; English, self-paced reading; manual advance, try before reveal

scene-root.name: Week 7 KP04 Inception and GoogLeNet (guided version)

scene-u01.name: Week 7 KP04 Inception and GoogLeNet (guided version)

p01-hook-title.name: p01-hook-title
p01-hook-title.text: Not by depth alone: can each layer use its kernels more cleverly?

p01-hook-ctx.name: p01-hook-ctx
p01-hook-ctx.text: VGG advances by going 'deeper', and parameters and computation explode together. Inception's answer: let kernels of different sizes work side by side within one layer.

p01-hook-vgg-t.name: p01-hook-vgg-t
p01-hook-vgg-t.text:
VGG: deeper and deeper
one kind of kernel per layer ($3\times3$)
about $138$ million parameters

p01-hook-inc-t.name: p01-hook-inc-t
p01-hook-inc-t.text:
One layer: $1\times1$, $3\times3$, $5\times5$ and pooling in parallel, joined along the channels
before the expensive large kernels, squeeze the channels with $1\times1$

p01-hook-q-t.name: p01-hook-q-t
p01-hook-q-t.text:
This unit answers four questions:
1. Why are going deeper and going wider both costly?
2. Why does the early module put four paths side by side?
3. What does a $1\times1$ convolution actually do?
4. How much computation and how many weights does reducing first save?

p02-motive-title.name: p02-motive-title
p02-motive-title.text: Why are going deeper and going wider both not free?

p02-motive-ctx.name: p02-motive-ctx
p02-motive-ctx.text: The Inception module and GoogLeNet come from the same work; the team was at Google, and the name also pays tribute to LeNet; GoogLeNet won ILSVRC 2014.

p02-motive-c1-t.name: p02-motive-c1-t
p02-motive-c1-t.text: With many parameters and too little labelled data, a model easily memorizes the training data.

p02-motive-c2-t.name: p02-motive-c2-t
p02-motive-c2-t.text: The larger the network, the longer it takes.

p02-motive-sp-t.name: p02-motive-sp-t
p02-motive-sp-t.text: Remedy: make the network sparser — do not fill every place with dense computation, put it only where needed. This echoes Occam's razor (keep it simple if you can).

p03-early-title.name: p03-early-title
p03-early-title.text: Why does the early module put four paths side by side?

p03-early-ctx.name: p03-early-ctx
p03-early-ctx.text: How to decide whether a layer uses $1\times1$, $3\times3$ or $5\times5$? Inception: put them all in and let the network choose.

p03-early-in-t.name: p03-early-in-t
p03-early-in-t.text: The same input (feature maps of the previous layer)

p03-early-pn0.name: p03-early-pn0
p03-early-pn0.text: related neurons cluster in a small group

p03-early-pn3.name: p03-early-pn3
p03-early-pn3.text: does not change the channel count

p03-early-pad-t.name: p03-early-pad-t
p03-early-pad-t.text: To be joined, every path must output the same side length, so padding keeps the convolutions from shrinking the size [Added].

p03-early-deep-t.name: p03-early-deep-t
p03-early-deep-t.text: The closer to the output, the more abstract the features and the larger the receptive field needed: deeper layers have more $3\times3$ and $5\times5$.

p04-1x1-title.name: p04-1x1-title
p04-1x1-title.text: A 1×1 convolution cannot see neighbours — so what does it do?

p04-1x1-ctx.name: p04-1x1-ctx
p04-1x1-ctx.text: Each position holds a vector of length $C_{\mathrm{in}}$, multiplied by a $C_{\mathrm{in}}\times C_{\mathrm{out}}$ matrix to give a new vector of length $C_{\mathrm{out}}$ (the example is [Added]).

p04-1x1-pos-t.name: p04-1x1-pos-t
p04-1x1-pos-t.text:
Position 1: $(1,\ 2,\ 3)$
Position 2: $(0,\ 1,\ 1)$
two positions, three channels

p04-1x1-u1-t.name: p04-1x1-u1-t
p04-1x1-u1-t.text:
1. Mix channels: at each position the channel values are linearly combined (VGG uses it occasionally).
2. Change the channel count: from many to few channels is dimensionality reduction.

p04-1x1-same-t.name: p04-1x1-same-t
p04-1x1-same-t.text: Three channels became two and the positions did not move at all: a $1\times1$ convolution works across channels at the same position and does not look at neighbours spatially.

p05-practice-a-title.name: p05-practice-a-title
p05-practice-a-title.text: Your turn: position 2, weights of 1×1, output channels

p05-practice-a-ctx.name: p05-practice-a-ctx
p05-practice-a-ctx.text: Work it out, then check. Assume input $28\times28\times192$.

p05-practice-a-q1-t.name: p05-practice-a-q1-t
p05-practice-a-q1-t.text: Position $2=(0,1,1)$ of the previous page through the same $3\times2$ kernel matrix: what is the output?

p05-practice-a-q2-t.name: p05-practice-a-q2-t
p05-practice-a-q2-t.text: Input $28\times28\times192$ with $64$ kernels of $1\times1$: how many weights? How many multiply-adds?

p05-practice-a-q3-t.name: p05-practice-a-q3-t
p05-practice-a-q3-t.text: The four paths of the early module have $64,128,32$ channels plus the $192$ kept by pooling: how many output channels after concatenation?

p05-practice-a-a1-t.name: p05-practice-a-a1-t
p05-practice-a-a1-t.text:
$(0+0+1,\ 0+1-1)=(1,0)$.
Three channels became two, positions unchanged.

p05-practice-a-a2-t.name: p05-practice-a-a2-t
p05-practice-a-a2-t.text:
Weights: $1\times1\times192\times64=12,288$.
Multiply-adds: $28\times28\times12,288=9,633,792$ (the $1\times1$ path of the early module).

p05-practice-a-a3-t.name: p05-practice-a-a3-t
p05-practice-a-a3-t.text:
$64+128+32+192=416$ channels.
(In the final module the pooling is followed by $32$ $1\times1$ kernels: $64+128+32+32=256$.)

p06-final-module-title.name: p06-final-module-title
p06-final-module-title.text: What does the final module add? Why reduce first?

p06-final-module-ctx.name: p06-final-module-ctx
p06-final-module-ctx.text: Problem of the early module: large kernels eat many channels directly, which is expensive; and max pooling does not change the channel count, so channels keep accumulating.

p06-final-module-why-t.name: p06-final-module-why-t
p06-final-module-why-t.text:
The expensive $3\times3$ and $5\times5$ eat $192$ channels directly, a large computation.
First squeeze the channels with $1\times1$ (reduction), then apply the large kernel.

p06-final-module-why2-t.name: p06-final-module-why2-t
p06-final-module-why2-t.text: Max pooling does not change the channel count; a $1\times1$ after it avoids too many output channels.

p07-cost-title.name: p07-cost-title
p07-cost-title.text: How much computation does reducing first save?

p07-cost-ctx.name: p07-cost-ctx
p07-cost-ctx.text: Take one GoogLeNet module (3a) as an example [Added]: input $28\times28\times192$; $1\times1$ with 64 kernels; $3\times3$ reducing to 96 first and then 128 kernels; $5\times5$ reducing to 16 first and then 32 kernels; pooling followed by a $1\times1$ with 32 kernels.

p07-cost-rat-t.name: p07-cost-rat-t
p07-cost-rat-t.text:
Early $303,464,448$, final $128,049,152$ multiply-adds:
early is $2.37$ times final, so the final is less than half.

p08-practice-b-title.name: p08-practice-b-title
p08-practice-b-title.text: Your turn: how many weights does reduction save in the 3×3 and 5×5 paths

p08-practice-b-ctx.name: p08-practice-b-ctx
p08-practice-b-ctx.text: Work it out, then check. Input $28\times28\times192$; the $3\times3$ path has $128$ kernels, reducing to $96$ first; the $5\times5$ path has $32$ kernels, reducing to $16$ first.

p08-practice-b-q1-t.name: p08-practice-b-q1-t
p08-practice-b-q1-t.text: $3\times3$ path: $128$ kernels of $3\times3$ eating $192$ channels directly, versus reducing to $96$ first: how many weights each?

p08-practice-b-q2-t.name: p08-practice-b-q2-t
p08-practice-b-q2-t.text: $5\times5$ path: $32$ kernels of $5\times5$ eating $192$ channels directly, versus reducing to $16$ first: how many weights each?

p08-practice-b-q3-t.name: p08-practice-b-q3-t
p08-practice-b-q3-t.text: Why do deeper Inception layers, closer to the output, have more $3\times3$ and $5\times5$?

p08-practice-b-a1-t.name: p08-practice-b-a1-t
p08-practice-b-a1-t.text:
Directly: $3\times3\times192\times128=221,184$.
Reduce first: $18{,}432+110{,}592=129,024$, which is $92{,}160$ fewer, only $58.3\%$.

p08-practice-b-a2-t.name: p08-practice-b-a2-t
p08-practice-b-a2-t.text:
Directly: $25\times192\times32=153,600$.
Reduce first: $3{,}072+12{,}800=15,872$, about one tenth.

p08-practice-b-a3-t.name: p08-practice-b-a3-t
p08-practice-b-a3-t.text: Closer to the output, features are more abstract and need a larger receptive field for broader spatial correlation; in shallow layers correlations cluster in small groups and $1\times1$ is enough.

p09-googlenet-title.name: p09-googlenet-title
p09-googlenet-title.text: How is the whole GoogLeNet put together?

p09-googlenet-ctx.name: p09-googlenet-ctx
p09-googlenet-ctx.text: Stack such modules layer by layer as the backbone.

p09-googlenet-pre-t.name: p09-googlenet-pre-t
p09-googlenet-pre-t.text: Input an image of $224\times224\times3$ and subtract the mean of each RGB channel (zero-centering), the same as VGG.

p09-googlenet-stack-t.name: p09-googlenet-stack-t
p09-googlenet-stack-t.text: Stacked Inception modules form the backbone: multi-scale parallel paths replace a single kernel size, and $1\times1$ reduction controls the computation.

p09-googlenet-relu-t.name: p09-googlenet-relu-t
p09-googlenet-relu-t.text: All convolutions (including those inside the modules) use ReLU.

p09-googlenet-no-h.name: p09-googlenet-no-h
p09-googlenet-no-h.text: What is not invented, and the design logic

p09-googlenet-no-t.name: p09-googlenet-no-t
p09-googlenet-no-t.text:
The source gives no number of layers, channels per layer or parameter count for GoogLeNet, and this unit does not invent them.
What is certain is the design logic:
1. multi-scale parallel paths replace a single kernel size
2. $1\times1$ reduction controls the computation
3. stacked modules deepen the network

p10-misconceptions-title.name: p10-misconceptions-title
p10-misconceptions-title.text: What is wrong with these four statements?

p10-misconceptions-ctx.name: p10-misconceptions-ctx
p10-misconceptions-ctx.text: Judge each one first, then read the correction on the right.

p10-misconceptions-c0-t.name: p10-misconceptions-c0-t
p10-misconceptions-c0-t.text: Both increase parameters and computation; a way to control them is needed.

p10-misconceptions-c1-t.name: p10-misconceptions-c1-t
p10-misconceptions-c1-t.text: It mixes channels at every position and can change the channel count.

p10-misconceptions-m2-t.name: p10-misconceptions-m2-t
p10-misconceptions-m2-t.text: 'Reduction makes the network unable to see clearly.'

p10-misconceptions-c2-t.name: p10-misconceptions-c2-t
p10-misconceptions-c2-t.text: Space is still handled by $3\times3$ and $5\times5$; $1\times1$ only compresses the channels linearly, with ReLU before and after.

p10-misconceptions-m3-t.name: p10-misconceptions-m3-t
p10-misconceptions-m3-t.text: 'Every layer has the same proportions of $1\times1$, $3\times3$, $5\times5$.'

p10-misconceptions-c3-t.name: p10-misconceptions-c3-t
p10-misconceptions-c3-t.text: Not fixed; deeper layers have more large kernels.

p11-quiz-a-ctx.name: p11-quiz-a-ctx
p11-quiz-a-ctx.text: The source's questions with all options; the source page marks answers, and the explanations follow the source's answers.

p11-quiz-a-q0-t.name: p11-quiz-a-q0-t
p11-quiz-a-q0-t.text:
What does the final Inception module add relative to the early design?
A. All kernels changed to $7\times7$
B. $1\times1$ reduction before $3\times3$ and $5\times5$ and after pooling
C. All $1\times1$ removed
D. Fully connected layers replace convolutions

p11-quiz-a-a0-t.name: p11-quiz-a-a0-t
p11-quiz-a-a0-t.text: Answer B. The final module adds $1\times1$ reduction before 3×3 and 5×5 and after pooling (Section 4).

p11-quiz-a-q1-t.name: p11-quiz-a-q1-t
p11-quiz-a-q1-t.text:
What is the main motivation of $1\times1$ convolutions in Inception?
A. Colouring images
B. Linearly transforming features, and reducing dimension before large kernels / after pooling to lower computation
C. To replace softmax
D. To force the use of LRN

p11-quiz-a-a1-t.name: p11-quiz-a-a1-t
p11-quiz-a-a1-t.text: Answer B. 1×1 transforms the channels linearly and reduces dimension before large kernels and after pooling, lowering the computation (Sections 3, 4).

p12-quiz-b-ctx.name: p12-quiz-b-ctx
p12-quiz-b-ctx.text: The source's questions with all options; the source page marks answers, and the explanations follow the source's answers.

p12-quiz-b-q0-t.name: p12-quiz-b-q0-t
p12-quiz-b-q0-t.text:
Which is correct about GoogLeNet?
A. Input $224\times224\times3$ with the RGB mean subtracted; stacked Inception as backbone; convolutions use ReLU
B. The input must be $32\times32$ grayscale
C. No ReLU at all, LRN instead
D. Only one Inception layer

p12-quiz-b-a0-t.name: p12-quiz-b-a0-t
p12-quiz-b-a0-t.text: Answer A. Preprocessing is the same as VGG, the backbone is stacked Inception modules, and convolutions use ReLU (Section 5).

p12-quiz-b-q1-t.name: p12-quiz-b-q1-t
p12-quiz-b-q1-t.text:
Why do deeper Inception layers closer to the output have more $3\times3$ and $5\times5$?
A. A larger receptive field is needed for more abstract features
B. Only shallow layers need large kernels
C. $1\times1$ is forbidden in deep layers
D. Max pooling can only follow the output layer

p12-quiz-b-a1-t.name: p12-quiz-b-a1-t
p12-quiz-b-a1-t.text: Answer A. The deeper, the more abstract the features, and the larger the receptive field needed (Section 2).

p13-summary-title.name: p13-summary-title
p13-summary-title.text: One sentence, plain words, formulas: what to take away from KP04

p13-summary-ctx.name: p13-summary-ctx
p13-summary-ctx.text: Close the slides and try to say the one-sentence version yourself.

p13-summary-one-t.name: p13-summary-one-t
p13-summary-one-t.text: The Inception module runs $1\times1$, $3\times3$, $5\times5$ and pooling in parallel, concatenates them along the channels, and adds $1\times1$ reduction before $3\times3$, $5\times5$ and after pooling, getting multi-scale features with less computation and fewer parameters.

p13-summary-plain-t.name: p13-summary-plain-t
p13-summary-plain-t.text: Like shooting a group photo with wide-angle, standard and telephoto lenses at once and stacking the photos. To keep the film from being too much and too expensive, first shrink the original, then hand it to the expensive lens.

p13-summary-fix-h.name: p13-summary-fix-h
p13-summary-fix-h.text: Corrections and choices relative to the source

p13-summary-fix-t.name: p13-summary-fix-t
p13-summary-fix-t.text:
1. The source gives no channel counts, layer counts, parameter counts or formulas; the $1\times1$ example, the multiply-add and weight formulas and the settings of GoogLeNet 3a are [Added].
2. Paths need padding to be concatenated, which is [Added].
3. Figures 13–15 of the source are not used.

p13-summary-next-h.name: p13-summary-next-h
p13-summary-next-h.text: The question for the next unit

p13-summary-next-t.name: p13-summary-next-t
p13-summary-next-t.text:
Inception and VGG both take an image in and output one class. If the task is not 'what is the whole image' but 'what is each pixel', the output must be as large as the input.
The next unit (KP05) looks at U-Net, built for segmentation.

p01-hook-nav.name: p01-hook-nav
p01-hook-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 01/13 · §1 Start · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p01-hook-cue0.name: p01-hook-cue0
p01-hook-cue0.text: Recall first: VGG went deeper and deeper, with one kind of kernel per layer.

p01-hook-cue1.name: p01-hook-cue1
p01-hook-cue1.text: Inception's way: several kernels side by side in one layer, with reduction before the expensive large kernels.

p01-hook-cue2.name: p01-hook-cue2
p01-hook-cue2.text: The four questions of this unit.

p02-motive-nav.name: p02-motive-nav
p02-motive-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 02/13 · §1 Motivation · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p02-motive-cue0.name: p02-motive-cue0
p02-motive-cue0.text: There are three ways to make a network more capable: deeper, wider, or both.

p02-motive-cue1.name: p02-motive-cue1
p02-motive-cue1.text: Cost 1: with many parameters and insufficient data, overfitting is likely.

p02-motive-cue2.name: p02-motive-cue2
p02-motive-cue2.text: Cost 2: the larger the network, the more the computation explodes.

p02-motive-cue3.name: p02-motive-cue3
p02-motive-cue3.text: So the direction is 'sparser': put computation only where needed (Occam's razor).

p03-early-nav.name: p03-early-nav
p03-early-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 03/13 · §2 Early module · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p03-early-cue0.name: p03-early-cue0
p03-early-cue0.text: The same input first goes through 1×1 convolution: in shallow layers related neurons often cluster in small groups, and 1×1 can handle them.

p03-early-cue1.name: p03-early-cue1
p03-early-cue1.text: Add 3×3 convolution: a larger kernel is needed when the related range is wider.

p03-early-cue2.name: p03-early-cue2
p03-early-cue2.text: Add 5×5 convolution: wider still, but large kernels are expensive and have many parameters.

p03-early-cue3.name: p03-early-cue3
p03-early-cue3.text: The fourth path: 3×3 max pooling, which does not change the channel count.

p03-early-cue4.name: p03-early-cue4
p03-early-cue4.text: The outputs of the four paths are concatenated along the channels, which makes the output 'multi-scale'.

p03-early-cue5.name: p03-early-cue5
p03-early-cue5.text: Concatenation requires equal side lengths (padding); the proportions of kernel sizes are not fixed, deeper layers have more large kernels.

p04-1x1-nav.name: p04-1x1-nav
p04-1x1-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 04/13 · §3 1×1 convolution · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p04-1x1-cue0.name: p04-1x1-cue0
p04-1x1-cue0.text: Look at the input first: two positions, three channels.

p04-1x1-cue1.name: p04-1x1-cue1
p04-1x1-cue1.text: The kernel matrix is 3×2: it linearly combines 3 channels into 2 channels.

p04-1x1-cue2.name: p04-1x1-cue2
p04-1x1-cue2.text: Position 1: (1,2,3) times the kernel matrix gives (4,−1). Position 2 is left for the next page's practice.

p04-1x1-cue3.name: p04-1x1-cue3
p04-1x1-cue3.text: So 1×1 convolution has two uses: mixing channels and changing the channel count; positions do not move at all.

p05-practice-a-nav.name: p05-practice-a-nav
p05-practice-a-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 05/13 · Practice · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p05-practice-a-cue0.name: p05-practice-a-cue0
p05-practice-a-cue0.text: Work it out yourself: the output at position 2, the weights and multiply-adds of 64 1×1 kernels, the channels after concatenation.

p06-final-module-nav.name: p06-final-module-nav
p06-final-module-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 06/13 · §4 Final module · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p06-final-module-cue0.name: p06-final-module-cue0
p06-final-module-cue0.text: The left is the early module: four paths in parallel, large kernels eating 192 channels directly, 416 channels after concatenation.

p06-final-module-cue1.name: p06-final-module-cue1
p06-final-module-cue1.text: The final module on the right keeps the same four paths.

p06-final-module-cue2.name: p06-final-module-cue2
p06-final-module-cue2.text: Place 1: before 3×3 and 5×5 add the green 1×1 reduction, squeezing the channels before the large kernel.

p06-final-module-cue3.name: p06-final-module-cue3
p06-final-module-cue3.text: Place 2: add a 1×1 after pooling as well; output channels drop from 416 to 256.

p07-cost-nav.name: p07-cost-nav
p07-cost-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 07/13 · §4 Computation · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p07-cost-cue0.name: p07-cost-cue0
p07-cost-cue0.text: First the 5×5 path: 32 kernels of 5×5 eating 192 channels directly need 120.4 million multiply-adds.

p07-cost-cue1.name: p07-cost-cue1
p07-cost-cue1.text: Reduce first: 1×1 reduces 192 to 16, then 5×5, about 12.44 million in total; 9.68 times fewer, roughly one tenth.

p07-cost-cue2.name: p07-cost-cue2
p07-cost-cue2.text: Whole module: early 303.5 million multiply-adds, final 128.0 million, less than half.

p07-cost-cue3.name: p07-cost-cue3
p07-cost-cue3.text: Output channels drop from 416 to 256 and weights from 387,072 to 163,328; all four paths remain, each just eating less.

p08-practice-b-nav.name: p08-practice-b-nav
p08-practice-b-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 08/13 · Practice · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p08-practice-b-cue0.name: p08-practice-b-cue0
p08-practice-b-cue0.text: Work it out yourself: weights of two paths directly versus reducing first, then think why deeper layers have more large kernels.

p08-practice-b-cue1.name: p08-practice-b-cue1
p08-practice-b-cue1.text: Answers: 221,184 versus 129,024 (58.3%); 153,600 versus 15,872; the deeper, the larger the receptive field.

p09-googlenet-nav.name: p09-googlenet-nav
p09-googlenet-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 09/13 · §5 The whole network · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p09-googlenet-cue0.name: p09-googlenet-cue0
p09-googlenet-cue0.text: Preprocessing is the same as VGG: a 224×224×3 image with each channel's mean subtracted.

p09-googlenet-cue1.name: p09-googlenet-cue1
p09-googlenet-cue1.text: The backbone is Inception modules stacked layer by layer.

p09-googlenet-cue3.name: p09-googlenet-cue3
p09-googlenet-cue3.text: The source gives no layer count or parameter count and we do not invent them; the three design logics are what is certain.

p10-misconceptions-nav.name: p10-misconceptions-nav
p10-misconceptions-nav.text: IDL 2026 FALL · Week 7 KP04 · 10/13 · Misconceptions · Manual: Next to advance / Prev to go back; reveal answers after you try

p10-misconceptions-cue0.name: p10-misconceptions-cue0
p10-misconceptions-cue0.text: Judge each statement first: all four sound like common sense, each wrong in one detail.

p10-misconceptions-cue1.name: p10-misconceptions-cue1

Why are going deeper and going wider both not free? · Cost 1: with many parameters and insufficient data, overfitting is likely.
Why are going deeper and going wider both not free? · Cost 2: the larger the network, the more the computation explodes.
Why are going deeper and going wider both not free? · So the direction is 'sparser': put computation only where needed (Occam's razor).
